value.markup:
Every setting the server and the command line read from the environment. A value in crombolo.config.ts wins over the environment, and the environment over the default. See the configuration guide for where to start.

Server

SettingDefaultWhat it does
NODE_ENV—`production` turns off the development conveniences: generated admin passwords, writable schema files, e-mail to the console and relaxed upgrade checks.
PORT8080The HTTP port. The application URL defaults to localhost on this port. A number.
CROMBOLO_SITE_NAMECromboloThe site's name, shown in the back office and used when a page is shared.
CROMBOLO_APPLICATION_URLhttp://localhost:<port>The site's public address, which invitation and password-reset links point at.
CROMBOLO_ROLEallWhat this process serves: everything, the back office and its API, or the public site alone. Splitting needs Postgres; a misspelt role stops the server. One of all, api, web.
CROMBOLO_NODE_IDhost:pidThis node's name, stamped on schema syncs, content changes and the upgrade history.
CROMBOLO_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_MB32The largest request body the server reads, media uploads included. A number.
CROMBOLO_INSECURE_COOKIESfalseDrops the secure cookie requirements, for a plain-http host that is not localhost. true or false.

Database

SettingDefaultWhat it does
CROMBOLO_DBsqliteWhich database engine the site runs on. One of sqlite, postgres.
CROMBOLO_SQLITE_FILEcrombolo.sqliteThe SQLite file, relative to the site, or `:memory:`.
CROMBOLO_POSTGRES_URL—The Postgres connection string. Required when the database is Postgres. Keep this secret: it is never shown back.
DATABASE_URL—Used as the Postgres connection string when `CROMBOLO_POSTGRES_URL` is unset. Keep this secret: it is never shown back.
CROMBOLO_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS15How long a content write waits for another before it gives up and answers 503. A number.
CROMBOLO_PG_DUMP—A shell command that backs up Postgres before a repair, an upgrade or a purge. It is given `CROMBOLO_BACKUP_STAMP` and `CROMBOLO_BACKUP_REASON`; without it those commands need `--backup-taken`.
CROMBOLO_UPGRADE_POLICYstrict in production, else pending-allowedWhether findings that need a person stop an upgrade. One of strict, pending-allowed.
CROMBOLO_VERSION_CLEANUPfalseRuns the hourly clean-up of old content versions. true or false.
CROMBOLO_VERSION_CLEANUP_KEEP_ALL_DAYS7The clean-up keeps every version newer than this many days. A content type's own policy wins. A number.
CROMBOLO_VERSION_CLEANUP_KEEP_LATEST_DAYS90After that, it keeps each day's latest version for this many days. A number.
CROMBOLO_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS365How many days the audit log keeps an entry. `0` keeps them all. A number.

Sign-in and secrets

SettingDefaultWhat it does
CROMBOLO_ADMIN_LOGINadmin@crombolo.localThe login of the first administrator.
CROMBOLO_ADMIN_PASSWORDgenerated in developmentThe first administrator's password, used only when the database is created. Unset in production, the site is set up in the browser. Keep this secret: it is never shown back.
CROMBOLO_SETUP_CODE—Guards "Set up your new site" in production: 16 or more characters, chosen by you. Remove it once the site is set up. Keep this secret: it is never shown back.
CROMBOLO_API_CLIENT_ID—An API client an unattended install creates in the administrators group; it starts `crombolo-back-office-`. With it, no password administrator is created unless `CROMBOLO_ADMIN_PASSWORD` is set.
CROMBOLO_API_CLIENT_SECRET—That client's secret, set together with the id. It is used once, when the client is created. Keep this secret: it is never shown back.
CROMBOLO_LOCAL_ADMINfalseCreates the password administrator even when an API client is set. Honoured only on localhost. true or false.
CROMBOLO_SECRET_KEY—Seals secrets kept in the database, such as a webhook's headers and two-factor keys; 32 or more characters. Features that need it are not offered without it. Keep this secret: it is never shown back.
CROMBOLO_USERNAME_IS_EMAILtrueA back office user's login is their e-mail address. true or false.

Back office and bundles

SettingDefaultWhat it does
CROMBOLO_BACKOFFICE_PATH/cromboloWhere the back office is served.
CROMBOLO_CSS_DIRcssThe stylesheets the Settings section edits, served at `/css/`.
CROMBOLO_SCRIPTS_DIRscriptsThe scripts the Settings section edits, served at `/scripts/`.
CROMBOLO_APPLY_BUNDLE_CONTENTtrueInstalling a bundle from the Marketplace also applies the schema, components and content it carries. true or false.
CROMBOLO_RUNTIME_INSTALLStrue, false with a schema storeThe Packages section installs and removes packages on the running site. Off, they are added to `package.json` and deployed. true or false.
CROMBOLO_MARKETPLACE_URLhttps://www.npmjs.com/search?q=keywords%3Acrombolo-bundleWhere the Marketplace sends someone browsing for bundles.
CROMBOLO_PACKAGE_KEYWORDcrombolo-bundleThe npm keyword a bundle publishes under to be found by the Marketplace.
CROMBOLO_NPM_REGISTRYhttps://registry.npmjs.orgThe registry the Marketplace searches, such as a mirror.

Schema

SettingDefaultWhat it does
CROMBOLO_SCHEMA_DIRschemaWhere the schema files live. Nothing is synced when the folder is absent.
CROMBOLO_SCHEMA_REVISION0Set by a deploy, to order deploys of the same schema version.
CROMBOLO_SCHEMA_CACHE_DIR<temp>/crombolo-schemaWhere a schema kept in cloud storage is copied to when the server starts.
CROMBOLO_SCHEMA_WRITABLEtrue unless production or with a schema storeWhether the back office may change the schema files. true or false.
CROMBOLO_SYNC_SCHEMA_AT_BOOTtrueSyncs the schema files when the server starts. Turn it off when a deploy runs `crombolo types sync` itself. true or false.

Components

SettingDefaultWhat it does
CROMBOLO_COMPONENTS_DIRcomponentsWhere the site's page views and components live.
CROMBOLO_COMPONENTS_CACHE_DIR.crombolo/componentsWhere components are copied so that an edit is picked up without a restart. Inside the site, and cleared when the server starts.
CROMBOLO_COMPONENTS_GATE_MS5000, 500 in developmentHow often a node looks for changed components, in milliseconds. A number.
CROMBOLO_COMPONENTS_SWAP_MS10000, 0 in developmentThe least time between two changes being picked up, in milliseconds. A save made in the back office is never held back by it. A number.
CROMBOLO_COMPONENTS_GENERATION_LIMIT250How many changes a node picks up before it stops taking more and keeps serving the last. A number.
CROMBOLO_COMPONENTS_KEEP3, all in developmentHow many earlier copies are kept on disk, for an instant return to one. A number.
CROMBOLO_RENDER_TIMEOUT_MS10000How long a page may take to render, layouts included, before it fails, in milliseconds. `0` for no limit. A number.

Media

SettingDefaultWhat it does
CROMBOLO_MEDIA_DIRmediaWhere uploaded files live on this disk, served at `/media/`.
CROMBOLO_MEDIA_STOREfilesystemWhere media files are kept. An unrecognised value falls back to the file system. One of filesystem, s3, azure.
CROMBOLO_MEDIA_PUBLIC_URL—A CDN in front of the media folder: browsers are sent there instead of being served by this server.
CROMBOLO_MEDIA_S3_BUCKET—S3: the bucket.
CROMBOLO_MEDIA_S3_REGION—S3: the bucket's region.
CROMBOLO_MEDIA_S3_ENDPOINT—S3: the endpoint, for an S3-compatible store such as R2, Spaces or MinIO.
CROMBOLO_MEDIA_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID—S3: the access key. Unset, the client's usual credentials are used.
CROMBOLO_MEDIA_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY—S3: the access key's secret. Keep this secret: it is never shown back.
CROMBOLO_MEDIA_S3_SESSION_TOKEN—S3: a session token, for temporary credentials. Keep this secret: it is never shown back.
CROMBOLO_MEDIA_S3_PREFIX—S3: a folder inside the bucket to keep media under.
CROMBOLO_MEDIA_S3_PUBLIC_URL—S3: a public address for the bucket, such as a CDN, that browsers are sent to.
CROMBOLO_MEDIA_S3_PRESIGN_SECONDS—S3: sends browsers to a signed bucket address that lasts this many seconds. Use this or a public address, not both. A number.
CROMBOLO_MEDIA_AZURE_ACCOUNT—Azure: the storage account.
CROMBOLO_MEDIA_AZURE_CONTAINERmediaAzure: the blob container.
CROMBOLO_MEDIA_AZURE_KEY—Azure: the account's key. Keep this secret: it is never shown back.
CROMBOLO_MEDIA_AZURE_SAS—Azure: a shared access signature, instead of the key. Keep this secret: it is never shown back.
CROMBOLO_MEDIA_AZURE_ENDPOINT—Azure: the blob endpoint, for a sovereign cloud or a local emulator.
CROMBOLO_MEDIA_AZURE_PREFIX—Azure: a folder inside the container to keep media under.
CROMBOLO_MEDIA_AZURE_PUBLIC_URL—Azure: a public address for the container, such as a CDN, that browsers are sent to.

E-mail

SettingDefaultWhat it does
CROMBOLO_EMAIL_PROVIDERnoneHow e-mail is sent. Without one, invitations, password resets and form e-mails are unavailable; development prints messages to the console. One of none, resend, postmark, ses, custom.
CROMBOLO_EMAIL_FROM—The sender address. Every provider needs it, and verifies its domain.
CROMBOLO_EMAIL_FROM_NAME—The name shown beside the sender address.
CROMBOLO_EMAIL_API_KEY—The provider's key: Resend's API key, Postmark's server token, or a bearer token for a custom endpoint. Keep this secret: it is never shown back.
CROMBOLO_EMAIL_URLthe provider's own APIThe address messages are sent to. Required for a custom endpoint, an override for the others. Must be HTTPS unless it is on this machine.
CROMBOLO_EMAIL_POSTMARK_STREAMoutboundPostmark: the message stream to send on.
CROMBOLO_EMAIL_SES_REGIONAWS_REGIONSES: the region to send from.
CROMBOLO_EMAIL_SES_ACCESS_KEY_IDAWS_ACCESS_KEY_IDSES: the access key, when it differs from the standard AWS one.
CROMBOLO_EMAIL_SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEYAWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEYSES: that access key's secret. Keep this secret: it is never shown back.
CROMBOLO_EMAIL_SES_CONFIGURATION_SET—SES: the configuration set that governs sending.
CROMBOLO_EMAIL_SES_ENDPOINTthe regional SES addressSES: a private endpoint to send through instead.

Members

SettingDefaultWhat it does
CROMBOLO_ALLOW_MEMBER_REGISTRATIONfalseLets visitors register as members of the site. true or false.
CROMBOLO_MEMBER_REGISTRATION_TYPEMemberThe member type a registration creates, by alias.
CROMBOLO_MEMBER_REGISTRATION_GROUPS—The member groups a registration joins, separated by commas. A comma-separated list.
CROMBOLO_MEMBER_SESSION_MINUTES20160How long a member's sign-in lasts, in minutes. The default is 14 days. A number.
CROMBOLO_MAX_FAILED_PASSWORD_ATTEMPTS5Failed member sign-ins before the member is locked out. `0` never locks out. A number.

Public site

SettingDefaultWhat it does
CROMBOLO_INDEXABLEtrueOff keeps search engines out entirely, for a staging site: robots are refused, there is no sitemap and every page asks not to be indexed. true or false.
CROMBOLO_SITEMAPtrueServes `/sitemap.xml`. true or false.
CROMBOLO_TRACK_REDIRECTStrueRenaming or moving a page records a redirect from the address it had. true or false.
CROMBOLO_DELIVERY_APIfalseTurns on the Delivery API, which serves content as JSON. true or false.
CROMBOLO_DELIVERY_API_KEY—The key that unlocks a private Delivery API, and previews of unpublished content. Keep this secret: it is never shown back.
CROMBOLO_DELIVERY_API_PUBLICtrueOff, every Delivery API request needs the key. true or false.
CROMBOLO_DELIVERY_API_MEDIAfalseThe Delivery API serves media as well as content. true or false.

Remote

SettingDefaultWhat it does
CROMBOLO_REMOTE_ENABLEDfalseLets `crombolo pull` and `crombolo push` reach this site. true or false.
CROMBOLO_REMOTE_ENVIRONMENTproductionThe name this site goes by for pull and push: lower case letters, digits and dashes.
CROMBOLO_REMOTE_PROTECTEDtrueA push here needs the protected-push permission. true or false.
CROMBOLO_REMOTE_APPROVALSfalseA push to a protected site waits for someone else to approve it. Needs `CROMBOLO_SECRET_KEY`. true or false.
CROMBOLO_REMOTE_MAX_UPLOAD_GB50The largest push or media file a client may upload, in gigabytes. Every other request keeps the usual body limit. A number.

Logging

SettingDefaultWhat it does
CROMBOLO_LOGS_DIRlogsWhere log files are written, a file a day, read by the back office log viewer.
CROMBOLO_LOG_LEVELinfoThe least severe level logged. One of trace, debug, info, warning, error, fatal.
CROMBOLO_LOG_TO_CONSOLEtrueLog events are also printed to the console. true or false.
CROMBOLO_TRACE_REQUESTSfalsePrints a line on the console as each request arrives and as it is answered. true or false.
CROMBOLO_HEAP_INTERVAL_SECONDS0Every this many seconds, prints the memory in use and the requests in flight. `0` is off. A number.

Command line

SettingDefaultWhat it does
CROMBOLO_BOOT_ATTEMPTS10How many times `crombolo start` tries to start the site, waiting longer each time, before it exits. A number. Read by the command line only.
CROMBOLO_ACTORthe account running the commandWho the audit log records for a command, for a pipeline acting for someone. Read by the command line only.
CROMBOLO_BUNDLE_PASSPHRASE—The passphrase for an encrypted content file, instead of being asked for it. Read by the command line only. Keep this secret: it is never shown back.
CROMBOLO_DEBUGfalseAdds the stack trace to an unexpected error. true or false. Read by the command line only.
CROMBOLO_TEMPLATES_DIRthe templates the command line shipsWhere `crombolo init` finds its site templates, for trying a changed one. Read by the command line only.

AWS credentials

SettingDefaultWhat it does
AWS_REGION—The AWS region, for SES e-mail and the Bedrock assistant when they set none.
AWS_PROFILE—The AWS profile the Bedrock assistant signs in with.
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID—A static AWS access key, for SES e-mail and the Bedrock assistant.
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY—That access key's secret. Keep this secret: it is never shown back.
AWS_SESSION_TOKEN—A session token, for temporary AWS credentials. Keep this secret: it is never shown back.
